candidates.buyer: Treasurers and volunteers of about 8,600 ASBLs (small, medium); also Agence du benevolat, communes and federations that support them
candidates.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
candidates.evidence: https://paperjam.lu/article/la-conformite-des-comptes-des-organismes-non-lucratifs-reste-inconnue (8,612 ASBLs at 30 June 2026; 1,403 annual-account filings accepted in six months; small volunteer groups struggle; no sanctions yet); search results on LBR/Webinaire ASBL, guichet/LBR RBE circulars and the Grant Thornton and Kehlen summaries of the 2023 law; ministry guide for medium ASBLs announced for autumn 2026 on myasbl.lu (https://myasbl.public.lu/)
candidates.existing: Competitor search (local language) found no Luxembourg-specific ASBL accounting/filing tool; only generic French or German association software (Yapla from EUR 24/month, OHME from EUR 20/month, easyVerein, Asso360, AssoConnect) whose Luxembourg compliance (plan comptable, RCS filing format, RBE) was not confirmed. State offers a good-practice guide, a small-association accounting guide on myasbl.lu and LBR helpdesk; accounting firms (Grant Thornton and others) sell services. Ministry says accounting templates are in preparation (parliamentary reply, text cut off).
candidates.name: ASBL annual-accounts and RBE compliance kit for small volunteer associations (law of 7 August 2023)
candidates.trigger: Law of 7 August 2023 on ASBLs and foundations: every ASBL must keep accounts proportional to size (small: simplified receipts and expenditures statement; medium: double entry) and file them with the RCS via the LBR portal (LuxTrust/eID); accounts approved within 6 months of year end, filed within the following month. 2025 accounts due 31 July 2026 for calendar-year ASBLs that aligned statutes in 2024; others from 2026 accounts (filed 2027); transition ended 23 September 2025. RBE declaration also mandatory. Compliance can only be measured in 2027; sanctions not yet applied to ASBLs.
candidates.unchecked: Whether the state ships free accounting templates (would reduce gap); filing XML/format accepted by LBR and whether third-party tools can submit; how many of 8,600 ASBLs are paying-capable; willingness to pay of volunteer treasurers (low ARPU, possibly federation/commune bulk sales); whether any Luxembourg fiduciary or association platform already offers it; sanction timetable for ASBLs.

candidates.unchecked: Bill content on recurring reports/registers for operators, final adoption and dates, number of small operators, existing dispatch/fleet software, competitor search not run.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Private households declare staff to CCSS via a simplified procedure on MyGuichet.lu (declaration within 8 days; CCSS computes gross, contributions and 10% flat tax, bills monthly, half-yearly statements via eDelivery). Free state portal covers it; no Luxembourg titres-services equivalent found. Nothing new beyond a weak idea.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No scrap-specific register found. Waste dealing/brokering and collection/transport need AEV authorization (law of 21 March 2012 on waste); some activities registration only. Unverified whether scrap dealers hold such authorizations and what registers they keep. See candidate C09.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Only the AML cash >= EUR 10,000 regime for dealers in goods (customer ID, internal organisation, FIU cooperation, AED supervision). No second-hand or pawnbroker register found. See C06.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Jewellers, gold and precious-metal dealers, diamond dealers and antique dealers are named in guichet.lu as subject to the cash >= EUR 10,000 AML duties, supervised by AED. EU AMLR cash cap of EUR 10,000 mentioned for 1 July 2027 (French source, not Luxembourg-specific, unverified). See C06.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: End-of-life vehicle regime is the grand-ducal regulation of 17 March 2003 (2006 press kit only). No current approval or register details found for Luxembourg. Unverified; see C10.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Cattle ID and herd register rules exist (bovine tracing, livestock register kept by keepers); new law of 2 April 2026 on animal health (bill 8300) sets operator registration/approval and public registers, with ALVA powers. Details of operator registers not read. Farmers/traders are few and the state keeps the database. Nothing concrete to build yet; see C08.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: ALVA approves slaughterhouses, cutting plants and meat-product plants (approval form exists); all food businesses need HACCP-based plan and ALVA registration. Content of self-control register not confirmed. Nothing new beyond generic HACCP tools.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: ALVA annual hive registration form (prefilled with prior year, hive locations, medicine order annex) and mandatory notification of foulbrood/varroa. Tiny, hobbyist market and the state form is simple. See C05 (weak).

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Since 1 January 2023 vets must report antimicrobial prescriptions/administrations for cattle, goats, horses, rabbits, sheep, fish, pigs and poultry online on MyGuichet.lu via a professional space certified by ALVA (grand-ducal regulation of 23 December 2022, art. 19-1). Small practice count; state portal is the channel. See C07 (weak).

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: AGE authorizations under the water law of 19 December 2008 for new boreholes/wells; AGE and communes running an inventory of private wells and boreholes (communal letter September 2025); abstraction tax declared on MyGuichet.lu (2026: EUR 0.158/m3 above 200 m3, EUR 31.60 flat up to 200 m3). One-off inventory plus free state declaration. See C04 (weak).

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: No national fixed septic emptying frequency or mandatory periodic inspection found; communal rules and subsidies (e.g. Stadtbredimus EUR 100 per emptying); waste hauliers need AEV collection/transport authorization or registration. Nothing concrete.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Lifts: annual examination by an approved body (grand-ducal regulation of 25 October 1999; law of 27 May 2016 on lifts); gas heating installations periodic check every 4 years (regulation of 14 August 2000); pressure equipment per ITM standard conditions. Current consolidated texts and the approved-body list not confirmed. Buyers are building owners/syndics and big landlords, not quiet; inspection bodies already hold the schedule. Not pursued.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Budget used on higher-ranked categories; only private-well angle (cat. 10) was seen. Communal water supply is run by communes and syndicates, not small private operators.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Law of 19 December 2014 on plant protection products plus grand-ducal regulation: certificates (distribution/advice, professional use) with limited validity and continuing training, ASTA renewal form (2024) asks storage address; distributors keep a register and sale invoices must carry date, product name/approval number, quantity. Final regulation text and ASTA current pages not confirmed. See C03.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Temp agencies need establishment authorization plus Labour Minister authorization (Guichet says valid one year; a secondary source says three years, conflict unresolved); temporary labour loan under Labour Code L.132-1 (ADEM notification for short loans per secondary source); user firms must not use unauthorized agencies. Few operators. See C11 (weak). Posting bill 7221 relates to K01/K04.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing usable found: no Luxembourg text on funeral-firm licensing or burial registers surfaced (results were Swiss/French). Burial deadline petition 3303 (2024) mentioned. Cemeteries are communal. Unverified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Law of 7 August 2023 on ASBLs and foundations: all ASBLs must file annual accounts with the RCS (via LBR portal, LuxTrust/eID), with 2025 accounts due 31 July 2026 for calendar-year ASBLs that aligned statutes in 2024; 8,612 ASBLs at 30 June 2026; RBE declaration also required (89.9% compliance at end 2023); small volunteer groups struggle (Agence du bénévolat); no sanctions yet and ASBLs excluded from LBR sanction phase starting 21 September 2026. No halal/kosher supervision rules found. See C01.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi: law of 5 July 2016, limited licences; bill 8624 (filed 2026, Chamber of Commerce opinion July 2026) would create 2,050 licences (850 taxi, 1,200 VLC), driver card, VLC licence and booking intermediary authorization; EU directive transposition deadline 2 December 2026 cited. Road haulage/bus: Community licence, vehicles over 2.5 t on annex, tachograph rules. See C02 and C12.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Market sales governed by communal rules (Luxembourg City and Remich examples) with written authorization for products sold; no national register. Money changers not searched (financial sector regulator domain). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Childminders (assistants parentaux): agrément from MENJE (law of 15 December 2017), max 12 children, contract, CSA provider recognition; reform bill 8686 (billing uniformisation, qualified tariff, income compensation, agency dageselteren supports; avis March 2026). Tattoo/piercing: hygiene law 2018 with notification of practitioners (details not read). Hunting: battue declaration to ANF 15 days ahead, hunting syndicates; no register found. Driving schools: nothing found. See C13, C14.

candidates.buyer: Small ASBLs (sports clubs, local associations, parent groups), their volunteer treasurers, and communes that fund them
candidates.category: 32. ASBL and foundation accounting and RCS/RBE compliance (also 17 and 23)
candidates.existing: Free official 'guide comptable de la petite association' and the MyASBL portal; accounting firms (e.g. Grant Thornton offers a pre-set budget template). No dedicated ASBL software found, but my competitor search was weak.
candidates.known_note: Related to K03/K06 only by theme (non-profit sector); different buyer and duty.
candidates.name: Small-ASBL accounts and filing assistant (cash statement, annex, budget, general-meeting minutes, RCS filing calendar)
candidates.trigger: Law of 7 Aug 2023: small ASBLs file an état des recettes et dépenses plus a simplified annex (grand-ducal regulation of 17 Feb 2025) and a budget. Accounts go to the general meeting within 6 months of year-end and to the RCS within a month of approval, kept 10 years. Transition ended 23 Sep 2025, so the first full-regime filings fell due 31 Jul 2026 for ASBLs that updated statutes in 2024. LBR sanctions phase starts 21 Sep 2026 but ASBL and foundations are excluded for now. Ministerial approval of gifts over EUR 30,000 needs accounts filed since creation.
candidates.unchecked: Number of ASBLs by size class. Whether small ASBLs pay for tools. Penalty for late filing. Whether Excel templates or fiduciaries already fill the gap. Local competitor search: one query returned no named software; a second search by vendor name is still needed.

candidates.buyer: Owners of small companies (SARL-S, one-person SARLs, sole traders registered in the RCS) who do not use a fiduciary, plus small fiduciaries managing many files
candidates.existing: LBR portal now shows defects to filers, plus a LBR compliance guide and information campaigns. Fiduciaries and domiciliation firms handle this today.
candidates.name: RCS/RBE data-compliance monitor for micro-companies and sole traders (LBR sanctions phase)
candidates.trigger: Law of 23 Jan 2025 strengthens LBR monitoring. From 21 Sep 2026 LBR sends a registered letter ('date T'), then a public warning (T+30 days), notes on extracts (T+60 days), EUR 40 a day up to EUR 3,600 (T+7 months), and strike-off (T+12 months), with referral to the public prosecutor and possible administrative dissolution. Applies to wrong, outdated, missing or non-filed RCS/RBE data.
candidates.unchecked: Share of entities with defects. Whether fiduciaries already cover the buyer. Competitor search not run (budget).

candidates.buyer: Licensed gardiennage companies (small number, many small), and the clients that hire guards for events
candidates.existing: Competitor search (planning software for guards, Luxembourg) found no named product. Generic workforce-scheduling tools exist but I could not check them.
candidates.name: Private security firm compliance and roster tool (agent approvals, contract-type rules, event-security licence, guard-dog rules)
candidates.trigger: Bill 8031 amending the law of 12 Nov 2002: new event-security activity, rules on guard dogs, fines EUR 500-50,000, and a ban on agency temps and sub-contracted self-employed guards (frontaliers-grandest gives 1 Nov 2026; unconfirmed). Each agent needs ministerial approval and clean criminal record.
candidates.unchecked: Final vote and in-force date. Number of licensed firms (the ministry list exists as a .doc). Whether large firms such as G4S dominate. Real pain beyond the contract-type switch.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: Biofuel incorporation and GHG-reduction duties (excise law of 17 Dec 2010, Environment Administration documentary-control guide, 'balances biocarburants') fall on operators placing fuel on the market and importers, not on forecourt operators. No station-level register or periodic filing found. Nothing usable for a solo founder.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No commodity-trading, milling or warehousing sector of note in Luxembourg. The nearest regulated product (wine) is screened under 31.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: No credit-union or savings-group sector found. The relevant small non-profit duty is ASBL accounting and filing under the law of 7 Aug 2023 (see 32 and candidate C1). Agricultural co-operatives not searched separately.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: CNS direct immediate payment (PID) is the main billing channel. About 49-57% of doctors and dentists use it, and traditional reimbursement was due to end on 1 Jan 2026 (the CNS says so; a July 2025 press piece says PID is still voluntary, unresolved). The medical convention expires on 31 Oct 2026 and the AMMD refuses the new one. State-run PID platform, no clear software gap. No PID or e-health duty found for labs or physiotherapists.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: Pseudoephedrine medicines became prescription-only from 1 Dec 2024 (Ministry of Health). No new narcotics-register law found. Legal base is the 1973 law and the 1974 grand-ducal regulation. Pharmacies are few and well served by existing software. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security (gardiennage) needs authorisation from the Minister of Justice, plus ministerial approval of each agent. Bill 8031 (amending the law of 12 Nov 2002) is late-stage: Council of State second complementary opinion 9 Jun 2026, committee report 2 Jul 2026. It adds event security, rules on guard dogs, fines of EUR 500-50,000 and a ban on agency temps and sub-contracted self-employed guards. One secondary source gives 1 Nov 2026 as the date (unconfirmed). Cleaning: no specific rule found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: On-site register of workers (Labour Code L.211-29, kept 5 years), ITM safety notice, health and safety coordination plan, posting declarations via free e-Détachement. SNSFP merged into ITM on 1 Jan 2025. No 2025 law creating a new register. Posting side is covered by K01 and K04.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Real estate agents and developers are supervised by the AED (law of 12 Nov 2004, extended in 2020). AED circular 792 of 26 Jan 2026 covers client identification. TCSP and domiciliation providers must register with AED, and SPF annual certification is due by 31 Jul. The co-ownership law of 1975 is being reformed (video general meetings, April 2025). Mostly handled by fiduciaries and compliance vendors.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Guest registration form (fiche d'hébergement): law of 28 Feb 2025 in force 1 Sep 2025, now fully digital through the free Lux Héberge app and MyGuichet, for every guest aged 15+. No sanction for late filing. No national tourist tax found. Short-term rentals: commune declaration, and an establishment authorisation above 89 days a year.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: No search spent (budget went to the country-specific categories). No Luxembourg-specific lead seen.

coverage.category: 31. Wine growers and Moselle wine estates (country-specific)
coverage.found: Institut viti-vinicole (IVV) runs the agricultural surface declaration and viticulture census. 244 holdings in 2024. Harvest and stock declaration rules not confirmed. Bill 8640 (excise law amendments, Chamber of Commerce opinion 25 Nov 2025) is not confirmed to touch wine. Market is tiny.

coverage.category: 32. ASBL and foundation accounting and RCS/RBE compliance (country-specific)
coverage.found: Law of 7 Aug 2023: three ASBL size classes. Small ones (under 3 FTE, income up to EUR 50,000, assets up to EUR 100,000) file a cash statement plus a simplified annex. Grand-ducal regulation of 17 Feb 2025 sets the annex. Transition ended 23 Sep 2025. Accounts due within 6 months of year-end, filed within a month of approval. LBR sanctions phase from 21 Sep 2026 under the law of 23 Jan 2025 (ASBL excluded for now). Free official guide at myasbl.public.lu.

coverage.category: 33. Short-term rental / furnished let operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: Commune declaration, establishment authorisation above 89 days a year, 89-day cap in residential zone 1, EU short-term-rental registration regulation. About 1,100 dwellings in short-term use (Jan 2026 parliamentary answer). Mostly private landlords. No new filing duty found.

coverage.category: 34. Construction and demolition waste (country-specific)
coverage.found: Waste law of 21 Mar 2012; bill 8482 amends it (status unknown). Building materials inventory required on demolition (Art. 26). Chambre des Métiers is asking for an exemption for small jobs. No register obligation for artisans confirmed.

coverage.category: 35. Tobacco, alcohol and cabaret licences (country-specific)
coverage.found: Customs (Douanes et Accises) grants tobacco and cabaretage authorisations under the 1989 cabaret law. Spot checks in 2025 found shops without a licence. Budget law 2025 set a minimum excise on new tobacco products. No periodic filing duty for small shops confirmed.

coverage.category: 36. Property managers (syndics) and co-ownership (country-specific)
coverage.found: The 1975 co-ownership law is being reformed (April 2025 ministerial answer; remote general meetings). The Groupement des syndics professionnels is in the working group. Syndic AML status unconfirmed. No bill text found.

coverage.category: 37. Company domiciliation and TCSP providers (country-specific)
coverage.found: AED registration and AML supervision of domiciliation; SPF annual certification due 31 Jul; AED circular 792 of 26 Jan 2026. Served by fiduciaries and established compliance vendors.
